measured_natural_decode_interpretation: compiler_ms does not track gold_len_tokens (21-token and 101-token gold records cost about the same); it tracks tokens_emitted from the decode's own trajectory. Per-token cost here (~90-150ms) is far higher than the flat ~0.6ms/step measured along a low-ambiguity gold-replayed path (see depth_scan), indicating cost concentrates at genuinely ambiguous branch points, not uniformly per token.

depth_scan.method: replay a record's own gold token sequence as _initial_prefix at increasing depth k, then measure exactly one more real _compiler_ltr_decode_one step from that depth (same session/state-interning machinery a multi-step decode reuses)
depth_scan.purpose: directly test the missing-memoization / recomputation-vs-prefix-length hypothesis: if _materialize_prefix's ancestor walk or the CompletionSession's state-interning/domain/witness caches regressed to redo work proportional to prefix depth, per-step cost would grow with k
depth_scan.note_k0_excluded: k=0 pays a one-off ~500ms make_grammar_state/Lark-parser construction cost unrelated to decode search (confirmed via cProfile: models/grammar.py:509 make_grammar_state / dsl/grammar/fastpath/engine.py:1128 engine_for_dsl frames), not decode-step cost.
depth_scan.conclusion: compiler_ms for one more step stays flat (~0.6-1.0ms) across an 8x growth in prefix depth (10 to 80 tokens) along a mostly-forced-closure path. Rules out a position-dependent / missing-memoization defect by direct measurement.

cprofile_natural_decode.interpretation: For 6 outer build_completion_forest calls (6 real decode-loop iterations), the witness search makes 40 top-level terminal_witness queries, 9513 recursive _eval expansions, 306 outgoing() calls (283 real forest-build cache misses), and 17199 feed_token_id calls. 283 forest builds / 40 witness roots is approximately 7 per root, consistent with node_budget=16 bounding each top-level candidate's exploration across a handful of live candidates per branch point -- bounded per branch point, multiplied by however many branch points the trajectory visits. No single call dominates; cost is the sum of many bounded, real Lark-parse-plus-semantic-state operations.

verdict_detail: The compiler-tree completion-forest/witness search's own bounds (node_budget, backtrack_limit, deadline checks, structural state interning) are intact, re-verified here with direct instrumented evidence rather than source review alone. A dedicated depth-scan found no position-dependent cost growth, ruling out missing-memoization / quadratic-in-document-length as the explanation. The real cost driver is branch-point count: a property of the actual decode trajectory (which candidate the specific trained checkpoint's ranking picks at each ambiguous grammar junction), not simply the record's gold text length. This reconciles with, and does not contradict, the metering-gap doc's real single-record numbers on actual campaign checkpoints (14.8s-38s/record) -- tens of seconds is the expected order of magnitude once a decode visits more than a handful of genuinely ambiguous branch points at ~50-500ms each.
what_this_session_does_not_claim: Because the gd6j83-c2/c3 campaign checkpoints are unavailable in this workspace, this session cannot prove those specific seed-100002 records' decodes are dominated by branch-point count as opposed to some other seed-specific effect. It establishes the general mechanism on real fixture content using the real production code paths, which is as far as reproduction can go without the frozen checkpoints.
